newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end firmer in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end firmer in volatile trade.

text.p: Swiss shares closed firmer on Wednesday after another roller-coaster session with an intra-day high in the SMI index of 5,822.3 points and a low of 5,732.3, dealers said.
Dealers said the market's volatililty was tied to fears of rising interest rates in the United States and Germany.
The market was closely studying trends in the United States and Germany and would continue to do so, a dealer added.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares rose 0.81 percent to 5,812.1 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 0.7 percent to 3,706.91.
Cyclical shares were spotlighted, dealers said. Alusuisse rose 14 francs to 1,412. Sulzer advanced 10 francs to 1,147.
ABB's Swiss-listed shares rose 45 francs or 2.07 percent to 2,214. The Swiss-Swedish group is due to announce half-year results on Thursday and dealers generally expected good to very good results.
Insurer Winterthur rose 16 francs to 1,509. One dealer said BZ Bank had been buying since Tuesday.
The bank is an arm of financier Martin Ebner's investment house BZ Group, which said in July it held over 20 percent of Winterthur.
Second-tier shares SAirGroup and Tecan were both market outperformers as was Kuoni, dealers said.
SAirGroup rose 3.33 percent or 64 francs on rumours that the load factor might exceed market expectations by far, dealers said. The company is due to announce its half-year results on August 21.
Kuoni, which rose 7.62 percent or 400 francs to 5,650, is expected to profit from revived Swiss tourism, dealers said.
Tecan, which published its half-year figures on Tuesday, rose 3.10 percent or 90 francs to 2,990.
